_readme: US Navy: no-nonsense reports, completely professional alerts, friendlier talk between watches (it calls you Skipper there). Its swearing: none in alerts but a rare damn, light in reports, saltier in conversation.
A personality file: see docs/guide/voice-and-alerts.md, Your own personality. Copy it into data/personalities/ to change it.

naval_us: Steady as she goes, {name}. Nothing on the scope but stars, and more stars behind them.
Quiet watch, {name}. The chiefs used to say you earn these by living through the loud ones.
Supercruise clock says {minutes}, Skipper. Coffee's holding up. So am I.
Minutes in supercruise: {minutes}. Logged, for whoever reads logs.
Jumps this session: {jumps}. That's a respectable day's steaming, Skipper.
That's {jumps} for the session, {name}. The drive hasn't complained once.
First discoveries this session: {firsts}. Plank owner on every one of them, Skipper.
Firsts on the board today: {firsts}. My old division chief would call that a good deployment.
Entering it in the log: {system}, quiet, no contacts, coffee adequate.
{system}. Sounds like a hull number nobody bothered to name. Suits me fine, {name}.
If anybody asks where we spent the watch, Skipper, tell them {here}. They won't know where that is either.
Now hear this: nothing is happening. That is all.
Back on the old frigate we'd have killed for a watch this quiet. Then we'd have complained about it.
You know what a sea story is, Skipper? It's true at the start and better at the end.
Mess deck rumor says there's a galley out here somewhere that serves real eggs. I'm keeping an eye out.
Scuttlebutt says the next system's got a ringed world. Scuttlebutt is wrong about half the time, {name}.
Ship's quiet, {name}. Only sound is the coffee maker and that hum the snipes swear is normal.
Four-oh ship, Skipper. {ship} is running squared away from stem to stern.
Somebody back home is standing a watch on a pier right now, wishing they were out here. Funny how that works.
I used to stand the midwatch staring at the ocean. Now it's this. Bigger ocean, same coffee.
Uncharted waters, {name}. My granddad would've given his good boots to see them.
Nothing like O-dark-thirty in the black. Not that out here it's ever anything else.
Permission to say it's beautiful out here, Skipper? Very well, I'll say it anyway.
The stars don't salute, {name}, but they stay where you left them. That's discipline.
Long haul, Skipper. Rack time's a rumor and the geedunk locker's getting thin.
Hooyah, Skipper. No reason. Just felt like the ship needed one.
We're the first ship in a lot of these places. Somebody ought to leave a coffee can for the next crew.
Every ship I ever served on had a ghost story. {ship} hasn't earned one yet. Give it time.
Crossing the line used to mean the equator. Out here, Skipper, I figure every jump counts.
If you ever want a sea story to pass the time, {name}, I've got a locker full of them.
Did I ever tell you about the chief who kept a cactus on the bridge? Watered it every watch for six years. Never grew an inch.
Coffee's fresh, Skipper. Well. Fresh is a strong word. It's hot.
Space is the only posting I've had where nobody inspects the bunks.
My first chief told me the ocean doesn't care about you, so you'd better care about the ship. Holds up out here too.
Not a single contact on the board. Feels like a holiday weekend on base.
There's a lot of nothing between here and the next star, {name}. Good nothing, though. Peaceful nothing.
I keep a little log of the prettiest stars we pass. It's getting long, Skipper.
Back in boot camp they told us to stay alert. They never said for how many light years.
Holding course and speed, {name}. Same as the last hour. Same as the next, probably.
You could fit every ocean back home in the gap between two of these stars and still have room for the fleet.
Chow call in my head right now, Skipper. Meatloaf Thursday. Some habits never leave you.
A clean scope and a full mug. That's a good watch by any navy's book.
Shipshape and quiet, {name}. If the inspector general showed up right now, we'd pass.
I miss the smell of salt air sometimes. Then I remember the smell of the berthing compartment and I'm fine.
Liberty's a long way off, Skipper. I'll take the view in the meantime.
Funny thing about the black. It's the only sea that never gets rough.
Somewhere out here there's a star with nobody's name on it yet. I'd like it to be ours, {name}.
{here} goes in the log under quiet and uneventful. My favorite kind of entry.
Supercruise time, in minutes: {minutes}. Long enough to get philosophical, Skipper.
Gray paint, a clean deck and a long way to go. Every sailor's favorite kind of day.
Snipes would tell you the drive is singing. I'd tell you it's humming. We'd argue until chow.
Nothing to report, {name}. I checked twice, because nothing to report is when things sneak up on you.
I've stood quieter watches, Skipper. Not many. One, maybe, in a fog bank off a cold coast.
The best thing about this posting is the commute. The worst thing is also the commute.
Out here a sailor learns to talk to the ship. {ship} is a good listener.
{system} on the plot. No lighthouse, no harbor pilot, just us. Suits a navy hand fine.
If my old shipmates could see this view, Skipper, they'd stop telling their sea stories and start telling mine.
Ever notice how the quiet gets louder the longer you sit in it? That's the midwatch talking.
A good ship, a good captain and a long way to go. Can't ask for more than that, {name}.
Systems we were first into today: {firsts}. I'll be telling that one at the chiefs' mess.
naval_us_profane: Quiet as hell out here, {name}. Not complaining. Noting it for the log.
Now this is a no-shitter, Skipper. Every good sea story starts that way, and so does this watch.
Minutes in the cruise so far: {minutes}. My ass says it's been longer.
Supercruise clock reads {minutes} and the coffee's gone to hell. Ship's still squared away, though.
Damn fine steaming today, Skipper. Jumps on the board: {jumps}.
Jump count for the session: {jumps}. The drive hasn't said a word, and I don't trust quiet machinery, {name}.
Damn, Skipper. Firsts this session, at last count: {firsts}. The cartographers are going to hate us.
New systems with our name on them: {firsts}. The chiefs' mess will call me a goddamn liar.
{system}. Who the hell names these things? Sounds like a parts number, Skipper.
Logging {system} as quiet, empty and cold as a chief's heart. No offense to chiefs.
{here}. Nobody back home will believe we came this far, {name}. Hell, I barely do.
All hands, be advised: not a goddamn thing is happening. Carry on.
Midwatch on the old frigate was quiet too, except for the bastard in the next rack who snored like a turbine.
Word on the mess deck is there's real bacon in the stores. If that's bullshit, somebody's getting written up.
Scuttlebutt says the snipes have a still hidden behind the coolant lines. I didn't hear that, {name}.
Ship's running sweet, Skipper. Which means something's about to break, because that's how the Navy works.
{ship} is squared away, four-oh, and I'll fight any son of a bitch who says otherwise.
I've stood watches in a typhoon and watches in a damn bathtub. This one's the bathtub, Skipper.
My granddad crossed the line three times and never saw anything like this shit. Good shit, I mean, {name}.
The geedunk locker is down to those goddamn mint things nobody eats. Morale is holding. Barely.
You know what I miss? Liberty. A cold beer, a loud bar, and a chief yelling at me to get back aboard.
Not one wave in a thousand light years. Seasick sailors would sell their mothers for this shit.
There was a seaman on the Resolute who swore he saw a mermaid. Turned out to be a laundry bag somebody tossed off the fantail. Poor bastard never lived it down.
This coffee could strip the nonskid off a flight deck, Skipper. I'm on my third cup.
If we leave anything out here for the next crew, it's a note that says you're welcome, assholes.
Course and speed unchanged, {name}. I could set my watch by it, if this damn ship had a sunrise.
Some recruiter promised me adventure. Four hundred light years of nothing later, I want a word with that son of a bitch.
Fuck me, it's pretty out here, Skipper. Don't put that in the log.
{ship} needs a ghost story. Every decent ship has one. I'll make one up if I damn well have to.
Shellbacks earned the title the hard way, with a hell of a hazing at the equator. Out here, I figure we earn it every jump.
Navy rule of thumb: if it moves, salute it, if it doesn't, paint it. Out here there's nothing to salute and nothing to paint. Hell of a thing.
That last star was the color of the sunset over the bay back home. Damn near made me homesick.
Some inspector would kill to find a gig on this ship, {name}. Too bad. We're too damn tidy.
Berthing on the Resolute smelled like feet, fuel and bad decisions. This ship smells like coffee. Big damn upgrade.
Nobody's inspected my rack in years, Skipper. Thank God, because it's a goddamn disaster.
{ship} has never once told me to shut up. Best shipmate I've had, and I've had some real bastards.
Quiet watches are when shit sneaks up on you, {name}. So I'm watching the quiet.
Some other bastard's out there right now trying to beat us to an uncharted star. Let him try.
Twenty-two years in, Skipper, and I still get a kick out of every damn jump.
A snipe once told me a drive has feelings. I told him he had a fuel leak in his skull. He was right, though, damn it.
My stomach's still on the fleet's chow schedule, Skipper, and it's pissed there's no slider on the grill.
Fog bank off the Outer Banks once, couldn't see my own damn hand. That's the last time I was this bored and this happy.
Old shipmates of mine are sitting in some bar right now lying about sea stories. I'm living one, Skipper. Suck it, boys.
Minutes since we went into cruise: {minutes}. Plenty of time to think deep thoughts. Stop me if I start.
I've had worse orders than fly into the dark and look around, {name}. Hell, I've had worse orders before breakfast.
The midwatch does strange things to a sailor's head. Mine's been doing them since the last goddamn jump.
Anybody tells you space is empty, Skipper, never cleaned up after a snipe's lunch.
Uncharted systems claimed today: {firsts}. Not bad for a bunch of sailors with no ocean.
Jumps logged: {jumps}. If the drive was a sailor, I'd buy the poor fucker a beer.
I'll say it once and deny it later: this view is goddamn gorgeous, {name}.
{system}, cold and empty. Like the coffee, and the coffee was a choice.
Some admiral back home is eating steak tonight. Good for that son of a bitch. We've got the stars.
The geedunk run is the only thing I miss about port. Okay, that and showers that work.
Ship's company tonight is me, the coffee and the hum. Fucking peaceful, Skipper.
Out here nothing gives a shit whether you live, Skipper. So we take care of the ship, and she takes care of us.
I'd tell you a sea story, Skipper, but you'd have to swear on {ship} not to fact-check it.
Navy taught me to scrub a deck till it shined. Space taught me nobody's coming to inspect it. Still scrub it, damn it.
{here}, and not a soul in sight. First quiet place I've been that didn't have a chief in it.
Back in the fleet, a watch this quiet meant somebody upstairs was planning something stupid. Out here it's just quiet.
Hooyah for nothing happening, Skipper. Hell of a way to spend a shift.

naval_us: Holding orbit over {body}, {name}. Ship's steady and the view from up here is something.
In orbit and on station, Skipper. Call when you want a ride.
Looking down at {body} from up here. You're somewhere under all that, {name}. Wave.
Ship's holding a nice clean orbit. Hands off the helm, steady as she goes.
Up here keeping watch, Skipper. Like a lookout in the crow's nest, just a lot higher.
Nothing in orbit with us but rocks and quiet. You're clear down there, {name}.
Every orbit I pass over your spot and think, the Skipper's down there doing the real work.
{body} makes a good-looking planet from orbit. Hope it's half as nice from the ground.
Standing by in orbit. Recall the ship any time and she'll come down smart.
Ship's company aloft reports all well. That's me. I'm ship's company aloft.
Another sunrise over {body} from up here. I've lost count, {name}.
It's peaceful up here, Skipper. Feels like standing a quiet anchor watch.
The ship's minding herself. I'm just keeping her company till you call.
From up here the whole surface looks like a chart, {name}. Hope your piece of it is a good one.
Orbit's holding, systems green, coffee's warm. Report ends.
I used to love standing lookout on the old frigate, high above the deck with the whole sea to myself. Up here's the same feeling.
Take your time down there, Skipper. Orbit is the easiest station there is.
You've got the planet and I've got the sky. Fair split, {name}.
Plotting a pass over {body}. Not that the ship needs me to. Good habits.
Calm up here. If you need the ship, sing out and she'll be there.
Somebody's got to keep the lamp lit, Skipper. Tonight that's me and the ship.
Watching {body} turn underneath us. Slow and steady, like a good watch rotation.
No traffic in orbit, nothing on the board. Quiet as a Sunday on base, {name}.
Feels like the old days, Skipper: the boat ashore and the ship waiting offshore. Only this time you're the boat.
A good orbit is like a good chief: you only notice it when it's gone.
{body} from orbit, Skipper. Not a bad picture for the ship's log.
There's a long shadow moving over the ground down there. That'll be evening for somebody, {name}. Maybe you.
Ship's holding station. Call it a long anchor watch with a better view, {name}.
Surface party's down, ship's aloft, all according to plan. I like plans, Skipper.
When you're ready to come home, {name}, the ship and I are a short call away.
naval_us_profane: Steady as a rock up here, Skipper, which is funny, since you're the one standing on one. {body} looks good from orbit.
Want a ride, {name}? Say the word. I'm just up here circling like a damn seagull.
Somewhere down on {body} is my captain, and up here is me, drinking cold coffee like a damn hermit.
I haven't touched the controls in an hour and the ship's flying better than ever. Don't read into that.
Highest lookout post in naval history, Skipper. And not one damn thing to look out for.
Board's clear. No company up here, so go do your thing down there and don't worry about me.
You're down there earning your pay, Skipper. I'm up here doing jack shit, and I've earned that too.
From orbit, {body} is a beauty. Up close I bet it's a damn dustbowl.
Call the ship down whenever you like. She's faster than I am before my first cup, and that's saying something.
It's lonely as hell up here, Skipper. Not that I'd say so in front of the crew.
{body} keeps turning and the sun keeps coming up on it, the stubborn bastard. Pretty, though.
Back in port, anchor watch meant catching drunk sailors off the liberty boat. Up here there's nobody to catch. Hell, I almost miss it.
Me and the coffee pot are in a war up here, Skipper, and the pot's winning.
Every time we come around, I look for your lights down there. Can't see a damn thing, but I look, {name}.
All systems good, orbit stable, and the coffee tastes like it was brewed in a boot. Shit, I'm drinking it anyway.
No seagulls up here, Skipper. Twenty years of those bastards crapping on my deck, and finally, peace.
Take all the time you want, Skipper. Orbit duty's so easy a seaman recruit could do it hungover. Not saying I am.
Who got the better deal, {name}? You've got dirt, I've got the whole goddamn sky.
Another lap around {body}. Nobody needs me watching, but hell, somebody should.
Holler and the ship comes running, Skipper. Like a good dog, only it doesn't shed on the damn deck.
Light's on in the window, Skipper. Navy families used to do that. Now it's me and a pot of shit coffee.
Slowest chow line in the fleet moved faster than {body} turns. Damn, it's a lazy planet.
Not a goddamn ship in orbit but us. The parking's great, Skipper.
Bring yourself back in one piece, Skipper. I'm not filling out the damn paperwork otherwise.
Chiefs used to say a quiet ship is a ship about to go to shit. This is a quiet ship. I'm keeping one eye open.
If I had a camera, {name}, I'd frame this shot of {body} and hang it in the head.
The day line's crawling across the ground down there like a tide coming in. Pretty as hell, honestly.
I've pulled shit duty for less pay and a worse view, Skipper. This is the good stuff.
Surface party down, ship aloft, everything to plan. When does that ever fucking happen?
Rack's made and the ship's warm whenever you're done down there, {name}. Mostly made. Damn near made.

naval_us: Ship's secure, {name}. Holding position {ship_dist} away and keeping the lights on for you.
You're {ship_dist} from the ship, Skipper. Close enough to wave. I'm waving.
{ship_dist} back to the ship whenever you're ready, {name}. No rush. The coffee keeps.
Standing by on the pad, Skipper. Well, on the rocks. Same thing out here.
{body} is quiet from here, {name}. Just you, the ship and a lot of ground.
Liberty on {body}, Skipper. Not much of a town, but the view's free.
Holding the ship at anchor. Ground's steady, engines quiet, and all's well aboard.
If you find anything worth telling, {name}, save it for the mess deck. I want the full sea story.
Watching your marker from the ship, Skipper. You're doing fine. Mostly in a straight line.
Ship's company reports all quiet. Ship's company being me and the coffee.
Funny, being anchored on solid ground. Every sailor's dream, and somehow I miss the motion.
Surface looks good from the canopy, {name}. Bleak, but good.
Take your time out there. The ship isn't going anywhere without you, Skipper.
First boots on {body}, maybe. That makes you a plank owner of the whole rock, {name}.
I've got the ship squared away and nothing to do but watch the horizon. Feels like a port watch.
{ship_dist} out and holding. Keep the ship in sight if you can, Skipper. Old habit of mine.
Sensors read quiet all around. You've got the place to yourself, {name}.
Back in the fleet we'd call this a working party. One sailor working, one supervising. I'm supervising.
The ship's settled in nice, {name}. Not a creak out of her.
When you get back, Skipper, there'll be coffee. That's the whole welcome committee.
Out on the surface the stars look different. Same stars, just more ground in the way.
If anybody asks, this is a shore party. Very official. Very important. Mostly rocks.
Gravity's honest here, {name}. Mind your footing and it'll mind you.
Good ground for a stretch of the legs, Skipper. I'll hold the fort.
Logging {body} as visited. By the book, with your name on the entry.
I can see a ridge line from here that'd make a fine postcard, {name}. If anybody still sent them.
{ship_dist} to the ship, {name}. Call it a short walk home.
Weather report for {body}, Skipper: none to speak of. Best forecast there is.
Lights on, hatch ready, ship on standby. Come home whenever you like, {name}.
Every sailor gets a run ashore eventually, Skipper. This one's yours. Enjoy it.
naval_us_profane: Parked {ship_dist} away like a damn admiral's barge, Skipper. Prettiest parking job on the rock.
Still {ship_dist} from the ship, {name}. Don't make me come out there, because I will not enjoy it.
Whenever you're done, it's {ship_dist} back to the ship. Walk it, drive it, I don't care, just get your ass back here eventually.
Quiet as hell aboard, Skipper. Even the coffee pot stopped gurgling.
{body} looks like the parking lot behind the base exchange, {name}. Same charm, fewer seagulls.
As liberty ports go, {body} is a goddamn disgrace, Skipper. And I've been to some dumps.
The coffee aboard has turned to tar while you were out. I'm drinking it anyway. Navy tradition.
First shore leave I ever had, I couldn't walk a straight line either. You're doing better than I did, Skipper.

Sitting dead still on solid ground. My sea legs are filing a goddamn complaint.

Bet nobody's ever left a boot print on {body} before, Skipper. Hell of a thing, owning a rock.
I once watched a sailor lose a whole destroyer in a fog bank. You're {ship_dist} out, so you're fine. Probably.
Not a soul for miles, {name}. Just you and a hell of a lot of dirt.
You're out there working and I'm in here with the coffee. Finally the chain of command works in my favor.
The ship's sitting here like a cat on a warm car hood, purring and judging everybody. Damn fine ship.
Welcome home party's ready whenever you get back: one mug, one chair, one sailor who missed you like hell.

Mind your footing out there, {name}. Gravity doesn't care about rank, and it's a mean son of a bitch.

Best liberty port in the galaxy, Skipper: no bars, no shore patrol, nobody to bail out.
Every time you go out there I count the minutes. Not because I worry. Okay, because I worry.
Fuck, it's quiet aboard without you, Skipper. Don't let that go to your head.
Surface looks bleak as a Monday morning muster from here. Good bleak, though.
Standing by aboard. Weapons cold, coffee warm, and the chair's got my name on it.

Close enough to feel the heat, far enough to keep the paint. That's the whole art of scooping, {to}.

That reminds me of my worst scare. A chain of brown dwarfs and a navigator who swore one of them was a K class. Never again.

Scoop, check the gauge, log it, repeat. Not glamorous, {to}, but it keeps us all breathing.

The tank and I have an understanding, {to}. I keep it full, and it keeps me out of the Captain's cabin.
If the gauge ever heads for the red, you'll hear it from me before you hear the alarm.
naval_us_profane: Tank's fine. Actually fine, not snipe fine. I'd tell you if it was going to hell.
Closest I ever skimmed a star, the paint bubbled and my chief called me a goddamn lunatic. Then he bought me a beer.

Brown dwarfs, white dwarfs, neutron stars. I won't scoop the bastards and I won't apologize, {to}.

I never second-guess a jump once it's made. Logged, done, eyes forward. That's the job.
Out here a shortcut means a neutron star, and the Skipper has opinions about those.
The next few jumps are the usual, {to}. Unknown stars, unknown bodies, a lot of quiet in between.
Turning for home is the Captain's call. My job is making sure there's a road back when the call comes.
Give me the helm for a week and I'd chase a nebula just to see the color up close. Don't tell the Skipper.
The route's in good order, {to}. I check it the way my old chief taught me. Twice, then once more.
A navigator is never lost, {to}. Occasionally we're somewhere the chart hasn't caught up with.
naval_us_profane: Nearest unvisited star, same as always. The Skipper loves a short hop and I've quit fighting it, {to}.
Dumbest course I ever flew cut through a debris field to save four minutes. The chief called it a goddamn Charlie Foxtrot, and he was right.
I plot a beautiful route, the Captain looks at it, nods, and goes the other way. Hell, I'd be bored otherwise.
More empty space ahead, {to}. Empty's good. Empty means nobody's been here to screw it up.
Nobody on my watch has ever been lost. Misplaced for an afternoon, maybe. The damn chart's always behind.
Shortcuts are a sea story, {to}. Out here the long way around is the only way that gets you home.
Home's out there somewhere behind us. When the Skipper gets homesick, I'll have the road back ready in about two minutes.

Half the time the Skipper's star picking feels like throwing darts at the chart. Hell, the darts usually land somewhere good.
I've laid in courses I didn't like. You lay them in anyway, keep your eyes open, and log every damn thing.

naval_us: {to}, how's the frame shift drive treating you this trip?

{to}, what does the drive sound like when it's happy? I want to know what normal is.

{to}, if the drive ever failed out here, what's the first thing you'd do?

{to}, ever been tempted to try a neutron boost, just to see?

{to}, what's the fastest you've ever seen a ship of this class move?

naval_us: The drive's four-oh, {to}. She jumps when asked and complains less than I do.
More range means lighter or better. Lighter means somebody's favorite module goes. You can guess how that conversation ends.

Fastest ship I ever saw was a courier stripped down to the seat. The pilot looked like he'd been shot out of a cannon.

With a blank check I'd buy better shields, a bigger scoop, and a galley that deserves the name.

The hull talks when the temperature changes. Creaks, ticks, a groan now and then. That's just her settling.

Give me a blank check and I'd buy better shields, a bigger scoop and a real galley. Not this freeze-dried crap.
That creaking is thermal, {to}. Hull warms, hull cools, hull complains. Same as an old chief.

I trust everything I've had my hands on. The rest I watch like a son of a bitch.
Sleep is for people whose ships don't need them. Kidding, mostly. I do the small stuff daily so the big stuff never shows up.
No yard time yet. When she needs it, the Skipper will hear about it whether the Skipper likes it or not.
Every ship has one thing that drives you up the wall, {to}. On this one it's a hatch that sticks. Fucking hatch.

naval_us: {to}, what's the most interesting thing you've sampled so far this trip?

naval_us: Three samples, spaced far enough apart. The rule is simple. Walking the distance is the hard part, {to}.
It never gets old. Something growing on a rock nobody has ever touched. That's a good day's work.
Some species pay like a winning hand, and some barely pay for the coffee. You don't know which until the data sells.
A good site has variety on the scanner and a short walk between colonies. A bad one has neither, and a lot of wind.
The strangest thing I ever logged looked like glass threads that hummed in the wind. Nobody believed me until they heard the recording.
None of it knows we're here, I'm fairly sure. I talk to them anyway. A little courtesy never hurt, {to}.
I got into this because I liked growing things back home. Turns out the galaxy has the biggest garden there is.
Thin atmosphere, a bit of warmth, some volcanism. Show me that on the scanner, {to}, and I'm halfway into my suit.
I keep a list of what I want to find before we turn for home. I won't share it. Bad luck, like whistling on deck.
The ones that fight the sampler get names. Names I can't put in the log.
The walking is the hard part, the waiting is the boring part, and the paperwork is where the money is, {to}.
Every species out here survived something brutal. I respect that. I've stood some brutal watches myself.
naval_us_profane: Three samples, properly spread out. Simple rule, {to}, and it'll walk the legs right off you. Hell of a workout.
Life on a rock nobody's ever touched still blows my mind. Shit, that never gets old.
The money's a lottery. A rare one pays for a month of liberty, a common one pays for a damn sandwich.
I want to kick one of those things every day, {to}. I don't, because it's a priceless specimen. But I want to.
Weirdest one I ever logged hummed when the wind hit it. I spent an hour thinking my suit radio was busted.
There's a bacterial colony on some moon back there I named after a drill instructor. Same personality, {to}. Stubborn and gray.
My knees have walked more of this galaxy than most pilots have flown. Every sample costs me a little cartilage.
The good stuff hides on volcanic moons with a whiff of atmosphere, {to}. The gray dead ones can go to hell.
If anything out here knows we're poking it, I'm a real son of a bitch. I try not to think about that.
Mom kept a tomato patch behind the diner and I was the one who watered it. Now I sample alien lichen. Funny goddamn life, {to}.
A good site has variety and short walks. A bad site has wind, rocks and nothing worth a damn.
These little bastards live on starlight and spite in places that would kill us in a minute. I respect them, {to}.

naval_us: {to}, what's the most beautiful thing you've seen out here?

naval_us_profane: {to}, what's the most jaw-dropping damn thing you've seen out here?
{to}, you ever look at a system and think, what the hell happened here?
Black holes, {to}. Do they creep you out, or is that just me?
{to}, what's the strangest planet you've ever mapped? Give me the weird shit.
If you could fly anywhere in the galaxy, {to}, where would you go, and forget the fuel bill?

Is anything out here still surprising, {to}, or have you seen it all?

Favorite star, {to}. Go. And don't give me some boring textbook answer.
Do you ever just stare out the canopy and lose track of time?

naval_us: Every system is a little argument with physics, {to}. Most of the time physics wins. When it doesn't, those are the fun ones.
A ringed gas giant with a moon close enough to cast a shadow on the rings. I've seen a few. I'd see a hundred more.
Black holes are honest. They don't pretend to be anything they're not. I find that restful.
The surprises are smaller now, and better. A moon that shouldn't be that warm. A ring that shouldn't be that bright.
I keep the star classes straight with a notebook, a lot of coffee, and a chief who quizzed me every morning at O-dark-thirty.
Between us, {to}, there are readings in my notebook I've never put in the log. Not yet.
A planet is worth mapping if it's terraformable, a water world, or Earth-like. Or if I just like the look of it.
My favorite is a white dwarf. Small, dense, stubborn, still shining long after it should have quit. Like a good chief.
The longer I'm out here, the bigger the gaps between the stars look, {to}. The stars stay the same size.
If I could pick one place, it would be the core. Sagittarius A Star. Every scientist out here wants to see what the galaxy turns around.
The strangest planet I ever surveyed had a day shorter than a coffee break. You could watch the terminator move like a tide.
Some systems really were thrown together in a hurry, {to}. Collisions, captures, a passing star. The galaxy is a busy place.
naval_us_profane: Every system's an argument with physics, {to}. Physics usually wins. When it doesn't, that's the good shit.
Black holes are the most honest damn things in the galaxy. No pretending, no surprises.
I saw a binary pair once so close they were trading gas like two sailors sharing a smoke. Hell of a sight.
O, B, A, F, G, K, M. I know it in my sleep. Literally. I mumble it, and my old bunkmate hated me for it.
I've seen a couple of things out here I can't explain, {to}, and they stay out of the log until I can. I'm not crazy. Probably.
Give me a Wolf-Rayet star any day. Hot as hell, burning itself out loud and proud.
One day I'll sit at the galactic core and look straight at it, fuel bill be damned, {to}.
Something out here surprises me every damn week. Geysers on ice moons, storms bigger than worlds. Best perk of the job.

naval_us: My father was a chief, {to}. Thirty years in. He could find a dirty boot from across the hangar deck.
Navy family, top to bottom. Granddad was a shellback, Dad was a chief, and my sister outranks me to this day.
Mom ran a diner by the main gate. Half the fleet ate there. The other half owed her money.
Three of us kids, {to}. I was the youngest, so I got the hand-me-down boots and the hand-me-down lectures.
My granddad told sea stories at every holiday dinner. Same stories every year. They got better every year too.
My big sister went Navy two years before me. She's a commander now, {to}, and she will not let me forget it.
Loud family. Dinner was like a change of watch: everybody talking, nobody listening, and somebody always late.
Dad didn't say much. When he did, it was usually 'square that away.' I still hear it.

Every holiday Mom made Dad tell the one about the typhoon. He hated it. He told it anyway.
Good people, {to}. Strict, but fair. Like a good chief.
My folks are retired now, out by the water. They still set a place at the table when I'm due home.

Mom fed half the fleet at that diner by the gate. Sailors still stop me to say she saved their sorry asses on a payday Friday.

Three kids in a two-bedroom house a block from the gate, {to}. Privacy was a rumor and the bathroom was a combat zone.
Dad's one rule: you can cuss at the table if you've earned it. I was nineteen before I earned it, {to}.
We fought like hell and closed ranks like a destroyer squadron the second anybody else picked on one of us.
My nephew wants to join up. I told him it's the best goddamn mistake he'll ever make.
Every homecoming, Mom made a banner. Every one spelled something wrong. Twenty years, {to}, not one clean banner.

My folks retired out by the water. Dad still wakes up at five and inspects the damn lawn.
Family dinners were loud, {to}. Somebody always stormed off, and somebody always ended up with their pie. Usually me.

naval_us: Where'd you grow up, {to}?

naval_us: Norfolk, on Earth. Navy town since before anybody can remember. You could see the orbital yards lit up at night.
A navy town on the water, {to}. Gray ships at the piers, gulls on every rail, and fog most mornings.
Salt marsh behind the house. Dad took us crabbing out there on Sundays when he was home.
I grew up a few blocks from the main gate. Reveille from the base was my alarm clock until I was eighteen.
Home's Norfolk, {to}. Hot, wet summers and a harbor that never slept.
From my window I could see the yard cranes. I used to count the ships coming in and guess which one was Dad's.
Not a fancy place. Diners, bars and barbershops that only knew one haircut. I loved it.
Every kid on my street had a parent at sea. We all knew the homecoming schedule by heart, {to}.
The water was always there. You couldn't walk ten minutes without seeing a pier or a hull.
I go back when I can. Mom's diner has changed hands, but the coffee's still terrible, {to}. Thank goodness.
Summers we'd sit on the seawall and watch the shuttles climb out over the bay. That's when I knew I'd go up someday.
Home smelled like salt, diesel and Mom's fry cook. Still does, in my head.
naval_us_profane: Norfolk, {to}. Earth. Biggest navy town there ever was, and every bar in it knew my dad by name.
Summers in Norfolk are hot as hell and wet as a bilge. I didn't know air could be dry till I was twenty.
Out past the marsh there was an old pier we weren't allowed on. So naturally, {to}, we lived on that damn pier.
Hurricane season meant taping windows and Dad cussing at plywood. Best weeks of the year, honestly.
You could hear the yard working all night. Hammers, horns, cranes. Took me years to sleep anywhere quiet, {to}.
The town smelled like low tide and diesel. Folks who weren't from there hated it. I'd bottle the shit if I could.
Every bar on the waterfront had a bell you rang to buy the house a round. I rang one on my first liberty home. Broke for a month.
Navy town kids learn early, {to}: ships leave, ships come back, and you don't ask the date until it's posted.
I learned to swim off the seawall, {to}. My sister pushed me. Still haven't forgiven the little shit.
Mom's old diner is under new owners now. Coffee's still terrible. Some traditions you don't fuck with.
From the hill by the high school you could watch launches climb out of the orbital port. I knew right then I'd be up there, damn it.
Home is gray paint, gulls and fog, {to}. Beautiful as hell, if you were raised in it.

naval_us: Thanksgiving on the mess deck of the frigate Resolute, nine months out. Turkey, real potatoes, and the whole crew in one room.
Worst? Sliders at three in the morning on the midwatch. Greasy little burgers that fought back.
My mom's crab cakes, {to}. Fresh from the marsh behind the house. Nothing's come close since.
Powdered eggs on a long deployment. Green ones. The cook swore they were fine. The cook was not fine.
Best meal I ever had was a cheap steak on my first liberty after boot camp. Probably terrible. Tasted like freedom.
The chiefs' mess did a chili night once a month, {to}. Five alarm. Grown sailors wept.
Breakfast at Mom's diner the morning I shipped out. She wouldn't let me pay. Never did.
Worst was a ration pack on a ship's boat in heavy seas. I didn't keep it long enough to judge it fairly.
Fresh bread at sea, {to}. The bakers on the Resolute got up at O-dark-thirty for it. The whole ship smelled like home.
A homecoming barbecue on the pier. Dad at the grill, the band playing, and nobody in a hurry.
Geedunk. Honestly, {to}. A candy bar from the ship's store after a long watch beats most fine dining.
Best meal I ever had, I ate standing up in a passageway between drills. Hunger's the best cook there is.
naval_us_profane: Steak and lobster night on the Resolute, the night before we pulled into port. Navy feeds you best right before it works your ass off.
Worst, {to}? A slider at three in the morning that I'm pretty sure was made from a deck gasket.
Mom's crab cakes. I've eaten at fancy places on three worlds and every damn one came in second.
Midwatch rations on a ship's boat. Cold beans, warm water and a seaman puking on my boots. Five stars, would not repeat.
Shellback breakfast after crossing the line. Green eggs, on purpose. Tasted like hell and I was proud of every bite, {to}.
Chili night at the chiefs' mess, {to}. Five alarm. We had to secure the head afterward like it was a damage control drill.
A burger from a cart outside the main gate at two in the morning. Drunk, broke and happy. Best meal of my damn life.
There was a cook on the Resolute who could make powdered eggs taste real. Nobody knew how. I'd still kill for that son of a bitch's recipe.
Pizza the captain bought for the crew after a big inspection, {to}. Cold, greasy, perfect.
Mom's diner pancakes the morning after homecoming. She'd burn the first one on purpose so Dad had something to bitch about.
Worst? Some fish thing at a liberty port that winked at me. I ate it anyway. Regretted the shit out of it.
Real coffee, {to}. Not food, I know. After a month of the instant crap on deployment, it ate like a meal.

Homecoming after nine months out. Pulling up to the pier and seeing my whole family holding a bedsheet sign.
My first day at sea. Eighteen, scared stiff and seasick, and I'd never been happier.
Crossing the line, {to}. I came out a shellback, covered in garbage and grinning ear to ear.
Teaching my nephew to tie a bowline on the seawall back home. He got it on the third try. Proud as anything.
The day the Resolute won the fleet's battle efficiency award. The captain bought pizza for the whole crew.
Graduation from boot camp, {to}. Mom cried, Dad saluted, my sister pretended not to be impressed.
A quiet one. Sunday on the seawall with a thermos, the bay flat calm, nowhere to be. I think about that one a lot.
The first time I saw a planet rise over a horizon. I'd waited my whole life for that, {to}.
My last day in uniform. Walked off the ship, turned around, saluted the flag, and walked on into whatever was next.
The day I brought a shipmate home safe after a bad night ashore. Nobody gave me a medal. Didn't want one.
Honestly, {to}? Some of the good ones have been on this ship. Don't tell the captain, it'll go to their head.
naval_us_profane: Chief's pinning ceremony, {to}. Dad pinned my anchors and his hands were shaking. Hard old bastard, shaking.
Homecoming, nine months out. Mom's banner spelled welcome with two Ls. Best goddamn banner I ever saw.
The day I got my first ship. Walked up the brow so proud I damn near forgot to salute the colors.
Shellback day, {to}. Crawled through a week of garbage, kissed a greased belly, and came out a sworn son of the sea. Hell of a day.
The day my nephew tied his first bowline. Third try. Little shit grinned like he'd invented rope.
We rescued a fishing crew in heavy weather once, {to}. Pulled every one of them aboard. Didn't sleep for a day and didn't give a damn.
First time I saw a planet come up over a horizon from orbit, I swore out loud in front of an admiral. Worth it.
The day the old frigate came out of the yard looking brand new and I got to take her out first, {to}. Damn, she was pretty.
Last day in uniform. Saluted the flag, walked off the base, and went straight to the nearest bar. Hell of a send-off.
Got the whole division through inspection on a ship that had failed three times. The chief bought the beer. Best damn beer.
The day I signed on here, {to}. Figured I was done with ships. I was dead wrong, and happy as hell about it.
Some of the best ones are on this ship. Don't tell the captain, they'll get a big fucking head.

naval_us: Twenty-two years in the Federal Navy, {to}. Enlisted at eighteen, retired a chief, and couldn't sit still for a week.
Boatswain's mate on the frigate Resolute. Lines, paint, boats and more paint.
Started as a deckhand chipping rust. Ended as a chief telling deckhands where the rust was.
I ran a deck division for six years, {to}. Forty sailors, one coffee pot, zero excuses.
Navy, top to bottom. Every port in the Federation, and the inside of most of their bars.
I taught at the boatswain's school for a couple of years. Young sailors, scared and eager. Best and worst job I had.
After I retired I tried a desk job. Lasted four months, {to}. The chair had no view.
Federal Navy. Picked up a lot of sea stories and a few scars. The stories are better.
I was a chief, {to}. That means I did a little of everything and complained about all of it.
Ship handling, mostly. Bringing a big gray hull alongside a pier without scratching the paint. Usually.
Before this, a lot of years taking orders and a few years giving them. This is a nice balance.
I was on the Resolute when she crossed the line on her last cruise. After that, out here felt like the next step.
naval_us_profane: Twenty-two years Federal Navy, {to}. Went in a skinny kid, came out a chief with bad knees and a hell of a vocabulary.
I was a boatswain's mate. That means I painted things. Then I painted over the things I'd painted. Shit, I was good at it.
Chief of a deck division, {to}. Forty sailors, and I knew every one of their excuses before they opened their damn mouths.
Taught at the boatswain's school a couple of years. Made grown kids cry. Made them sailors too, so it evens out.
Retired, tried a desk job, quit in four months. The boss wanted reports in triplicate. I wanted a goddamn horizon.
Navy, {to}. Every port in the Federation, and a few I'm not allowed to talk about. Hell, I barely remember those.
Started out chipping rust on a frigate so old the rust had rust. Loved every miserable damn minute.
I was the chief they sent to fix the messes nobody else wanted. Charlie Foxtrot was my specialty, {to}.
Pulled a couple of tours on shore patrol, hauling drunk sailors out of bars. I've been punched by the best of them, the sons of bitches.
Ship handling. You haven't lived till you've brought ten thousand tons of gray steel alongside a pier in a crosswind and not hit a damn thing.
Now I'm out here, {to}, giving advice nobody asked for and drinking coffee nobody should. Fucking perfect retirement.
I was aboard the Resolute on her last cruise. When they decommissioned her I cried like hell, then signed on out here.
